description:
FILED s540 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-13) on the USER's word (paraphrased): the first measurement (#4787, docs/cpan-speed-comparison-s540.md) found that the board's 33x is compile, not run -- so redo the measurement doing just the run time.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE MEASUREMENT: in #4787 the run phase was 8 % of PCL's CPU (162 s of 2,154 s: 110 s in PCL, 52 s in subprocesses) against perl's WHOLE 64.9 s -- but perl's 64.9 s includes perl's own compile of the test file and its modules, so the run-vs-run ratio is not known yet, and the per-file run numbers were small differences of large load-inflated totals (CPU time is not load-proof on this box: 2.1-2.5x at load 8+).

WHAT TO MEASURE
1. Per board file (the files that run to their plan with perl's ok count: 638 at #4787), the RUN PHASE on both sides: PCL from the first statement of the program to exit (everything transpiled, compiled and loaded before the clock starts -- tools/board-timing.pl has the phase boundaries; add a mode that reports only the run phase and repeats it N times in one warm state), perl from the end of its compile phase to exit (an INIT / CHECK timestamp, or perl -c subtracted: say which and show it agrees on ten files).  Subprocess time listed separately on both sides.
2. A QUIET BOX for every number that is reported (heavy.sh bench, chunks of at most 15 minutes, best of 3 with the spread); nothing normalised from a loaded pass.
3. The table: per distribution and per file, perl run s, PCL run s, the difference in ABSOLUTE seconds and the ratio; the sum over the board; the distribution of ratios (how many files under 1x, 1-2x, 2-5x, over 5x).
4. WHERE: the ~25 files with the most absolute run-phase excess, from at least 8 distributions, profiled (sb-sprof :cpu and :alloc; bytes consed and GC time beside the seconds) with the Perl construct behind each hot function named.  #4787's run-phase rows are the starting list to confirm or refute with clean numbers: JSON::PP encode / decode 4.6x with no single hot spot (#4967), fork +3.4 ms (#4965), Symbol::gensym 81 us (#4964), a match / s/// on a long string paying the whole length (#4966), string-eval compile (#2421 -- decide and SAY whether an eval's compile counts as run time: for the program it does).
5. THE LIST: things that are slow at RUN time, ranked by seconds over the board, each with the discriminating measurement taken and a task filed -- the same shape as #4787's section 4; cross-read with docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md so a lever both found is named once.

WHEN: after s540d has merged (the local-module compile default #4986, tr/// #4981, the constant fold #4982 and the `$|` probe #4983 all change run or load numbers) and preferably after #4962 (the TAP layer precompiled) and s540e (the shims) -- measure the tree those leave, and name the sha.  Since MAIN-READY-92 the sub-call frame is cheaper (call rows 8-42 % faster): the #4787 run numbers predate it.

DELIVERABLE: docs/cpan-runtime-comparison-sNNN.md + baselines/board-runtime-sNNN.tsv (a `# taken-at:` line: sha, date, load) + the filed tasks.  No change under Pl/, cl/, lib/.  Flag any file whose PCL run phase is under half of perl's (a possible silent skip) and read three of them.
subject: SPEED (USER s540): redo the CPAN board time measurement for the RUN PHASE ONLY -- perl vs PCL per file with compile / load / transpile taken out, the heaviest run-phase files profiled, the list of what is slow at RUN time
